**Finding: Deviation (critical) — INDEMN**

**What I found.** Section 12 contains indemnities in both directions, so this is not a "missing" clause — but TrueLink's side (12.b, p0073/p0075) is limited to claims "arising out of any breach by TrueLink of this Agreement or any failure by TrueLink in the performance of any of its obligations or agreements hereunder." That is a breach-of-contract indemnity only.

**Why it fails the fallback.** The playbook's fallback floor is a Vendor IP indemnity with usual exclusions and remedies. There is none here:
- No indemnity for third-party claims that the Interface / Hosting Services / Support Services infringe or misappropriate IP.
- The only infringement language in the document runs *against* us — a Client warranty on Client Content (§8e, p0055) and a Client covenant not to infringe TrueLink IP (p0024).
- By contrast, the Client indemnity at 12.a is expansive (Client breach, acts causing TrueLink default under System/Credit Repository Agreements, Web Site/Client Content "without regard to any knowledge limitation," and product/service injury).

The liability cap (p0077) is confined to Sections 3, 4, 7 and 11, so it does not backstop this gap either.

**Redline (validated, ok:true).** Inserted a new 12.c after p0075 giving TrueLink a defend-and-indemnify obligation for (i) IP infringement by the Interface/Services/deliverables, (ii) TrueLink's breach of law, (iii) unauthorized access to or disclosure of Client Content/Confidential Information caused by TrueLink, and (iv) TrueLink's gross negligence or wilful misconduct — with standard notice, control-of-defence (no adverse settlement without consent) and cooperation mechanics, plus carve-outs for Client Content and Client modifications/combinations.

I deliberately made the minimal edit: 12.a is left untouched even though it sits wider than the preferred "Customer content and breach of law" formulation, and I flagged the super-cap as a discussion point in the comment rather than drafting it in.
